theorem: An algebraic skew lift A with det(A)=det(I-C*C) requires the transfer determinant to be a square in the source coefficient ring.
smallest_falsifier: For scalar C=[x], det(I-C*C)=1-x^2 has simple roots at plus and minus one and is not a polynomial square.
doubling_control: The canonical skew doubling J(B) has Pf(J(B)) equal up to sign to det(B), and det(J(B))=det(B)^2; it does not take a square root.
revised_target: Find a source symmetry forcing compatible square factorizations of finite-cutoff transfer determinants, or abandon the Pfaffian recovery route.
status: universal finite algebraic no-go; no RH proof
